newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour calls GDP data "poor", bad for jobs.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour calls GDP data "poor", bad for jobs.

text.p: Opposition Labour Party finance spokesman Michael Cullen described New Zealand June quarter GDP data on Friday as "poor" and said slower growth was impacting on employment.
Production-based GDP grew 0.3 percent in the June quarter, the lowest quarterly rate since September 1992, and by 2.6 percent for the year.
Cullen said manufacturing activity had fallen on an annual basis in each of the past two quarters, and the farm sector had seen a decline in five of the last eight quarters.

"The manufacturing and agricultural sectors are vital to New Zealand's economic wellbeing. The fact they are in decline is a worrying signal, even to (Finance Minister) Bill Birch and his advisors, that all is not well in the New Zealand economy," he said in a statement.
Cullen added: "We have seen clear signs that the slowdown in economic activity is now beginning to impact on employment. Today's figures will only serve to extend this effect."
He said the governing National Party was going into a general election on October 12 with unemployment rising and economic activity falling.
